pipeline.camera_qa_reason: Calibration references include clinical crops that are not representative camera captures. Formula and ROI processing remain fully enabled.

noise_floor_pinned_metrics.methodology: Unlike this file's other metric bands (pigment_load, localized_redness, etc.), which use a uniform +/-5.0 tolerance around a human-reviewed 'confirmed' value, these three metrics' min/max are simply the CURRENT pipeline's own output on each photo, widened by that metric's own measured 2-SD scan-to-scan noise floor from tool/analyze_repeatability.py (texture_smoothness=5.4, glabellar_wrinkle_depth=6.4, wrinkle_load=3.7; see METRIC_NOISE_FLOOR_2SD in main.py), clipped to [0, 100].
noise_floor_pinned_metrics.caveat: These bands are PINNED TO CURRENT FORMULA BEHAVIOR, not validated against clinical/visual judgment of the actual photos the way the confirmed values elsewhere in this file are -- nobody has reviewed whether 'clear_face scores 72.6 for texture_smoothness' is a CORRECT score, only that it is what analyze_skin_patch produces today. Their sole purpose is to catch an accidental regression in these three formulas before a deliberate fix; they must not be treated as ground truth, and are expected to change (a new confirmed value, likely with a much narrower band) once texture_smoothness's and glabellar_wrinkle_depth's known score-amplification issue is actually fixed -- see the investigation that found two real repeatability sessions on the same, unchanged face produced texture_smoothness means approximately 70% apart (28.2 vs 47.9) despite the underlying raw signal ('energy') moving only about 20%, traced to var_p80/lap_p80 each contributing to the score twice (directly via n_var/n_lap and indirectly via texture_energy -> n_energy).
